statement.p: Let g(x)=\frac{1}{s\sqrt{2\pi}}e^{-\frac{(x-m)^2}{2s^2}}\text{,} where s>0\text{.} Find the range of x values for which g'(x) is positive.

The exponential factor is always positive, so the sign of g'(x) is determined by -(x-m)\text{.} Therefore, g'(x)>0 when x\lt m\text{.}
